version.changelog: Simplify setup, point to ToyBridge README, add Buttplug.io guidance

llm.summary: This skill clearly does what it says, but it controls an intimate physical device through an unauthenticated local bridge and relies on mutable external setup code.

dimensions.detail: macOS Bluetooth and a local HTTP bridge are proportionate to the stated BLE-control purpose, but the documented plaintext HTTP interface on port 8888 has no token, server identity check, or stated bind restriction, which is under-scoped for physical device control.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs users to follow an external ToyBridge setup guide and run 4-bridge/server.py, but the reviewed skill does not pin a commit, release, checksum, or vendored bridge implementation. That makes the effective executable dependency mutable after review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent commands are narrowly aimed at vibrate, stop, and status, and intensity is documented as 0-100. However, the skill tells the agent to issue bash curl commands directly to a fixed endpoint and provides no authentication, session duration cap beyond timed-session stop guidance, or explicit user confirmation before activation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cross-session persistence, backdoor, scheduler, or memory-writing behavior appears in the reviewed skill. The bridge is user-started and long-running while the terminal remains open, with local account, network, and Bluetooth privileges inherited from the user environment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent and disclosed: natural-language control of a Venus/Cachito BLE vibrator. The concern is that this is immediate physical actuation of an intimate device, with no prominent consent boundary, first-use confirmation requirement, or safety warning in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you understand that OpenClaw may directly activate the connected vibrator. Use it only with the informed consent of the person using the device, keep the stop command available, run the bridge locally with restricted network exposure, and prefer a pinned or reviewed bridge version before running external setup code.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The physical device-control capability is expected for this skill, but the artifact-backed lack of explicit consent and safety language is a real Review concern because commands can cause immediate intimate-device actuation.
[E1] expected: The curl POST sends an intensity value to the documented local bridge, not demonstrated credential or PII exfiltration. This finding is downgraded as data-exfiltration evidence, while the unauthenticated actuator-control channel remains relevant.
[T08] expected: Using a bridge server is expected for the skill, but the artifact directs users to mutable external code without integrity pinning, so the executable behavior is not fully represented by the reviewed package.
[T09] expected: The plaintext HTTP interface is part of the intended local-control path, but the absence of documented authentication or endpoint identity checks is materially under-scoped for controlling a physical device.
